newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia forms anti-Hanson unit for Asia -report.
newsitem.headline: Australia forms anti-Hanson unit for Asia -report.

text.p: Australia has set up a special diplomatic unit to counter race row politician Pauline Hanson's negative impact in Asia, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
The Australian newspaper said the unit would target Asian media and international news agencies to combat the negative image of Australia fuelled by Hanson's rising prominence.

The unit, to be called Images of Australia, would also be involved in assessing the regional impact of government decisions and how to sell those decisions in Asia, the newspaper said without citing sources.
It said the unit will aim to paint Australia as a sophisticated, technologically advanced and culturally diverse country, with a strong commitment to Asia.
The latest move follows a secret campaign by the foreign affairs department to discredit Hanson, an independent politician, throughout the region.

Department sources told Reuters in June that the department had been ordered to run an anti-Hanson campaign, translating speeches and other information discrediting her and giving it to foreign governments and media.
Hanson sparked a divisive national race row last year when she warned Australia was in danger of being swamped by Asians and attacked welfare for native Aborigines.
Prime Minister John Howard has been widely criticised for failing to act swiftly and firmly to counter Hanson's rise.
But Trade Minister Tim Fischer and Foreign Minister Alexander Downer have rejected her policies, warning they fuel intolerance and jeopardise Australian trade and prosperity.

Major opinion polls show support for Hanson's One Nation party between seven and eight percent -- enough to make her the third force in domestic politics and deliver an influential block of parliamentary seats if that is maintained to the next election, due by mid-1999.
